transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. As you all know, we have a preliminary-injunction hearing in three weeks, and I need to approve our response strategy before the motion papers are finalized. Before I sign off on anything, I need each of you to put your cards on the table. I want to hear about any material evidence we have — or don't have — any business constraints I should be aware of, and any proposed filing commitments you think we need to make. I don't want surprises after I've approved the strategy. So let's go around the room. Who wants to start?

While reviewing a forensic image that was delivered after the strategy-memo cutoff, I found the former employee's signed confidentiality agreement along with logs showing that 4,800 files — including source code and deployment scripts — were copied to an external drive. These supplemental findings have not yet been added to the motion outline. In my view, the signed agreement and the 4,800-file evidence significantly strengthen our case and make an expedited forensic inspection of the competitor's systems necessary. I recommend we request that inspection in the motion and file a supplemental-evidence filing to incorporate these findings.

The 30-day customer-transition period is something we'll need to build into the scope of the injunction we request. transcript.text:
Thank you both. This is exactly the kind of transparency I needed before approving the strategy. Let me synthesize what I'm hearing and make sure we're aligned.

Ethan, the signed confidentiality agreement and the 4,800-file transfer logs are significant additions. I want those incorporated into the supplemental-evidence filing and reflected in the motion outline before anything is finalized. I also agree that the forensic inspection is well-supported by this evidence — if we have logs showing source code and deployment scripts were copied to an external drive, we have a strong basis to ask the court to inspect whether that code is now embedded in the competitor's hosted product.

Nadia, the 30-day customer-transition carve-out is a hard constraint I'm going to respect. The client has made their position clear, and I won't approve a strategy that doesn't account for it. I also agree with your point about drafting the transition language explicitly and upfront — not as an afterthought. The client needs to see and approve the full injunction framework, including the carve-out, before I sign off.

So here's what I'm prepared to approve in principle: a preliminary injunction motion that includes the supplemental-evidence filing, requests an expedited forensic inspection of the competitor's systems, and contains an explicit 30-day customer-transition carve-out that preserves service continuity for existing hosted customers. The injunction would not shut down the customer-facing service during the transition period. The forensic inspection and the transition carve-out will be drafted as complementary provisions, not competing ones.

Before I formally settle this strategy, I want to make sure we haven't missed anything else. Is there anyone else in the room who has material evidence, business constraints, or proposed filing commitments I need to hear? If not, I'll move to approve this framework and we can get the revised motion outline drafted this week.
